source_caption_text:
“Stronger” was way ahead of its time when Kanye dropped it in 2007

Released in 2007, Kanye West’s “Stronger” felt completely different from what was dominating rap at the time. Built around Daft Punk’s “Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger,” the song brought electronic production into hip-hop in a way that felt natural rather than forced.

What made it stand out was how Kanye kept the attitude and energy of a rap record while building the entire song around pounding synths, distorted vocals and futuristic production. It showed that a rap song didn’t have to stay within the usual formula to connect with a massive audience.

“Stronger” went on to become one of the defining sounds of the late 2000s. Its success helped make synth-heavy, electronic-influenced production much more common in mainstream rap, opening the door for the genre to become even more experimental and crossover-friendly.
